description: Industrial effluent and tailing runoff polluting river water used for drinking and farming.
Groundwater exceeds permissible fluoride levels leading to widespread dental and skeletal fluorosis.
Post-harvest crop spoilage forces distress sales at extremely low rates during peak harvest.
Heavy unpaved coal haulage causes respiratory illnesses and ambient PM10 spikes in roadside settlements.
Wild elephant herds enter paddy fields damaging standing crops and posing risks to villagers.
Lack of local processing for Mahua and Lac forces tribal gatherers into exploitative seasonal migration.
High prevalence of iron deficiency anemia in tribal blocks due to dietary and water absorption barriers.
Poor storm-water management leads to regular waterlogging and sewer backflow during monsoon downpours.
Mining pits depress the regional water table drying up nearby dug wells and domestic handpumps.
Unstable mine waste dumps risk slope failure and landslides during heavy rain near settlements.
Rural students particularly girls drop out due to distance terrain and absence of public transit.
Workers operate without dust suppression leading to chronic respiratory failure and undiagnosed silicosis.
Farmers lack supplementary micro-irrigation when rains pause leading to recurring crop failures.
Underground smoldering fires destabilize residential ground and release toxic benzene and sulfur fumes.
Deep forest blocks lack fiber or 4G backhaul stalling public ration distribution and online welfare delivery.
Rural households burning unprocessed wood in poorly ventilated rooms suffer from chronic respiratory illness.
Remote livestock farmers suffer low conception rates due to unmaintained liquid nitrogen supply chains.
Unmetered hooks and decaying rural distribution lines cause brownouts and extreme fiscal losses for discoms.
Ground-level tube wells tap into arsenic-rich strata causing skin lesions and long-term toxicity.
Rural primary health centers lose serum potency during grid outages worsening snakebite mortality.
Tribal youth lack foundational curriculum and reading materials printed in native scripts like Ol Chiki.
Thermal power station ash dykes breach into local soil degrading farm fertility with heavy ash deposits.
Fresh fish caught from large reservoirs spoil during transit before reaching major urban markets.
Pipe culverts on rural link roads choke with debris and wash away cutting off village access.
Remote tribal homes lack basic warming facilities for low-birthweight newborns prior to clinic transfer.
Sericulture farmers rely on local middlemen who pay arbitrary prices for unprocessed cocoons.
Community water bodies silt up heavily reducing storage depth and drying out well before summer.
Dry leaf-litter fires go undetected for days in inaccessible hill tracts wiping out undergrowth and wildlife.
Unsegregated open dump yards catch fire regularly billowing dioxins and smoke into nearby towns.
Lateritic upland soils bind phosphorus and micronutrients severely depressing upland pulse crop yields.
